chunks: From him, from Ali, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Whoever honors Allah by swearing an oath by Him, Allah will give him good better than what was taken from him."

key_terms.أَجَلَّ: To honor, glorify, or show reverence
key_terms.ذَهَبَ: What was taken, lost, or given up

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for honoring Allah when taking an oath?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*'s chapter on oaths, this narration highlights the spiritual economy of *ikhlās* (sincerity), where reverence for the Divine Name acts as a catalyst for divine recompense. It suggests that the 'loss' incurred by swearing—whether the immediate act or the potential distraction—is outweighed by a superior, often unseen, blessing granted by Allah to those who treat His name with utmost respect.
